Then, when God, glorified is He, commanded them to avoid much suspicion, He forbade them from spying, saying, ﴿And do not spy﴾. *Al-tajassus* (التَّجَسُّسُ) is searching for what is concealed from you of the faults and private matters of the Muslims. God, glorified is He, forbade them from searching for people's defects and shortcomings.

The majority read ﴿tajassasu﴾ with the *jim* (بِالجِيمِ), and its meaning is what we have mentioned. Al-Hasan, Abu Raja' and Ibn Sirin read it with the *ha'* (بِالحاءِ).

Al-Akhfash said: Neither of them is far from the other, because *tajassus* with the *jim* is searching for what is concealed from you, and *tahassus* with the *ha'* is seeking news and searching for it.

It was also said: *tajassus* with the *jim* is searching, and from it comes the saying "a man is a *jasus*" (spy) when he searches out affairs. With the *ha'* it is what a person perceives through some of his senses.

It was said: with the *ha'* it is what a person seeks for himself, and with the *jim* it is to act as a messenger for another. This was said by Tha'lab.

﴿And let not some of you backbite others﴾. That is: let not some of you speak of others in their absence with what would displease them. *Al-ghibah* (الغِيبَةُ, backbiting) is that you mention a man with what he dislikes, as in the hadith of Abu Hurairah, established in the Sahih, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what backbiting is?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "Your mentioning your brother with what he dislikes." It was said: "What if what I say is true of my brother?" He said: "If what you say is in him, then you have backbitten him, and if it is not in him, then you have slandered him."

﴿Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?﴾ He, glorified is He, likened backbiting to eating carrion, because the dead person does not know that his flesh is being eaten, just as the living person does not know of the backbiting done about him. Al-Zajjaj mentioned this meaning.

This passage contains an indication that a person's honour is like his flesh: just as eating his flesh is forbidden, so is overstepping against his honour. There is, in this, a warning against backbiting (al-ghība), a rebuke to the one who commits it, and a strong condemnation of him, which is clear. Human nature recoils from eating human flesh, and the human disposition finds it repugnant, quite apart from its being forbidden by the Law. Thus ﴿فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ﴾ ("so you have disliked it"). Al-Farra' said: "Its implied reading is: ﴿فَقَدْ كَرِهْتُمُوهُ﴾ ('so you have indeed disliked it'), so do not do it." The meaning is: just as you dislike this, avoid mentioning your brother with evil in his absence. Al-Razi said: "The fa' (so) is in the sense of a response to a statement, as if he had said: 'None of you would love to eat the flesh of his brother; so you have disliked it, then.'"

Abu al-Baqa' said: "It is coordinated with an omitted element, its implied meaning being: 'This was presented to you, so you disliked it.'" ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ ("And fear Allah") by abandoning what He has commanded you to avoid. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ ("Indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance, Merciful") toward whoever fears Him, for what has passed from him of sin and of opposing the command.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others transmitted from Anas, who said: It was said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "If only you would visit Abdullah ibn Ubayy." So he set off to him, riding a donkey, and the Muslims set out walking, and the land was salty (sabakha). When he reached him, [Abdullah] said: "Keep away from me! By Allah, the smell of your donkey has harmed me." A man from the Ansar said: "By Allah, the donkey of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is better in smell than you!" Then men from his people became angry on behalf of Abdullah, and his companions became angry on behalf of each of them, so there was striking between them with palm-stalks, with hands and with sandals. Then there was revealed concerning them: ﴿وَإِن طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا﴾ ("And if two groups of the believers fight...") and so on.

Something similar has been related through other channels.

Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi transmitted from Ibn Umar, who said: "I have not felt anything in myself as much as I felt about this verse: that I did not fight this rebellious group as Allah commanded me."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas concerning the verse, who said: Allah commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers that when a group of believers fights, they should call them to the judgement of Allah and do justice between them. If they respond, he judges among them by the judgement of the Book of Allah until the wronged one is given justice. Whoever refuses to respond among them is a rebel (baghin), and it is incumbent upon the leader (imam) of the believers and the believers to fight them until they return to the command of Allah and acknowledge the judgement of Allah.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿وَإِن طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا﴾ ("And if two groups of the believers fight..."), who said: There was fighting with sandals and staves, so He commanded them to reconcile between the two.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi transmitted from Aisha, who said: "I have not seen anything like what this nation has turned away from in this verse: ﴿وَإِن طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا﴾ ('And if two groups of the believers fight, then make reconciliation between them')."

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Muqatil concerning His saying: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِّن قَوْمٍ﴾ ("O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people") that he said: It was revealed concerning a people from Banu Tamim who mocked Bilal, Salman, Ammar, Khabbab, Suhayb, Ibn Fuhayra and Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfa.

Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad, Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Dhamm al-Ghiba, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman transmitted from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿وَلَا تَلْمِزُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ﴾ ("And do not defame one another") that he said: Let none of you slander another.

Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari in al-Adab, the authors of the Four Sunan, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab, transmitted from Abu Jabira ibn al-Dahhak, who said: "It was revealed concerning us, the Banu Salama: ﴿وَلَا تَنَابَزُوا بِالْأَلْقَابِ﴾ ('And do not insult one another by nicknames'). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, and there was not a man among us except that he had two or three names. Whenever he called one of them by one of those names, they would say: 'O Messenger of Allah, he dislikes it!' So there was revealed: ﴿وَلَا تَنَابَزُوا بِالْأَلْقَابِ﴾."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted something similar from Ibn Abbas.

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn Abbas, who said: Mutual insulting by nicknames is that a man has committed evil deeds, then repented of them and returned to the truth, and Allah forbade that he be reproached for what had preceded from his deeds.

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud concerning the verse, who said: If a man was a Jew and then embraced Islam, and [another] would say to him: "O Jew! O Christian! O Magian!", and would say to a Muslim man: "O sinner (fasiq)!"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman transmitted from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِّنَ الظَّنِّ﴾ ("O you who have believed, avoid much of suspicion"), who said: Allah forbade the believer to suspect ill of a believer.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others transmitted from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech. Do not spy, do not seek out secrets, do not compete one with another, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, and be servants of Allah as brothers. A man should not make an offer upon the offer of his brother until he marries or leaves [the matter]."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab transmitted from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا﴾ ("And do not spy"), who said: Allah forbade the believer to pursue the faults (awrat) of a believer.

Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shayba, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab transmitted from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Mas'ud was brought word, and it was said: "This is so-and-so, whose beard is dripping with wine!" Ibn Mas'ud said: "We have indeed been forbidden to spy, but if something becomes apparent to us, we will take it."

Traditions have also come down forbidding the pursuit of the faults of Muslims and spying upon their defects.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab transmitted from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَعْضًا﴾ ("And let not some of you backbite others") to the end of the verse, who said: Allah has forbidden that a believer be backbitten about anything, just as He forbade carrion.

The traditions on the prohibition of backbiting are very numerous and well known in the books of hadith.

The commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 49, verses 13–18:

His saying: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾. They are Adam and Eve. The intended meaning is that they are equal, since they are connected by one lineage, and since one father and one mother gather them together, and there is no place for boasting among them through their lineages. It was also said that the meaning is: each one of you is from a father and a mother, so all are equal. ﴿And We made you peoples (shu'ub) and tribes (qaba'il)﴾. Shu'ub is the plural of sha'b, with a fatha on the shin, and it means a great tribal group, like Mudar and Rabi'ah. Qaba'il are less than that, like Banu Bakr from Rabi'ah and Banu Tamim from Mudar.

Al-Wahidi said: This is the view of a group of the exegetes. They were called sha'b because of their dispersal (tasha''ub) and gathering, like the branches (shu'ab) of a tree. Sha'b is one of the words with opposite meanings: one says sha'abtuhu when one gathers it, and sha'abtuhu when one scatters it. From this, death is called shu'ub, because it scatters. As for ash-shi'b with a kasra, it means a path in a mountain.

Al-Jawhari said: ash-sha'b is what branches out (tasha''aba) from the tribes of the Arabs and non-Arabs, and its plural is ash-shu'ub.

Mujahid said: ash-shu'ub are the distant in lineage, and the qaba'il are below that.

Qatadah said: ash-shu'ub are the lineage of the nearer ones.

It was also said: the shu'ub are the Arabs of Yemen from Qahtan, and the qaba'il are from Rabi'ah, Mudar and the rest of Adnan.

It was also said: the shu'ub are the branches of the non-Arabs, and the qaba'il are the branches of the Arabs.

Abu 'Ubayd related that the sha'b is larger than the qabilah, then the qabilah, then the 'imarah, then the batn, then the fakhdh, then the fasilah, then the 'ashirah.

What supports the view of the majority that the sha'b is larger than the qabilah is the saying of the poet:

Tribes from peoples, among whom there is no noble one who is counted, nor any well-born one.

The majority read ﴿li-ta'arafu﴾ with a light ta', and its origin is li-tata'arafu, so one of the two ta's was deleted. Al-Bazzi read it with a shadda on it, by idgham (assimilation). Al-A'mash read it with two ta's.

The lam is connected to ﴿khalaqnakum﴾: that is, We created you thus so that some of you would know one another.

Ibn 'Abbas read ﴿li-ta'rifu﴾ as the imperfect of 'arafa.

The benefit of mutual acquaintance (ta'aruf) is that each one of them is attributed to his own lineage and does not claim to be from another.

The intended meaning of this is that Allah, glory be to Him, created them thus for this benefit, not for boasting about their lineages and claiming that this people is better than that people, this tribe is more noble than that tribe, and this clan is more honourable than that clan.

Then He, glory be to Him, gave the reason for what the speech implies of the prohibition against boasting, and said: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most righteous of you﴾. That is, the distinction among you is only by piety (taqwa). Whoever is clothed with it is the one deserving to be more noble than the one who is not clothed with it, and more honourable and more excellent. So leave what you are engaged in of boasting about lineages, for that does not necessitate nobility, does not establish honour, and does not require superiority.

The majority read ﴿inna akramakum﴾ with a kasra on inna. Ibn 'Abbas read it with a fatha, meaning: because the most noble of you. ﴿Indeed Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of every thing known, including your deeds, ﴿All-Aware﴾ of what you conceal and what you disclose; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

When He, glory be to Him, mentioned that the most noble of people with Allah is the most pious of them towards Him, and the root of piety is faith (iman), He mentioned what the Arabs used to claim of faith in order to establish for them nobility and excellence, and He said: ﴿The Bedouins say: "We have believed."﴾ They were Banu Asad, who showed Islam in a year of drought, wanting charity. So Allah, glory be to Him, commanded His Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, to respond to them, and He said: ﴿Say: "You have not believed"﴾. That is, you have not affirmed with a sound affirmation that comes from conviction of the heart, sincerity of intention, and tranquillity. ﴿But say: "We have submitted"﴾, that is, we have surrendered (istaslamna) out of fear of killing and captivity, or out of greed for charity. This is the description of the hypocrites, for they showed submission outwardly while their hearts did not believe. For this reason He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾. That is, what you have shown with your tongues was not in agreement with your hearts, but was merely a saying with the tongue without sound belief or sincere intention. The sentence is either a new sentence to confirm what precedes it, or it is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal). In (lamma) there is the meaning of expectation (tawaqqu').

Al-Zajjaj said: Islam is the manifestation of submission and acceptance of what the Prophet brought, and by it blood is protected. If with that outward manifestation there is conviction and affirmation in the heart, then that is faith and its possessor is a believer.

He has removed these people from faith by His saying: ﴿And faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾, that is, you have not affirmed, and you have only submitted to protect yourselves from killing. ﴿But if you obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ with sound obedience proceeding from sincere intentions and hearts that affirm, not hypocritical, ﴿He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds﴾. It is said: lata yalitu, when it decreases; and latahu yaliituhu and yalutuhu, when it reduces it. The meaning is: He will not reduce anything of your deeds for you.

The majority read ﴿yalitkum﴾ from lataha yaliituhu, like baa'a yabee'uhu.

Abu 'Amr read ﴿la ya'iltkum﴾ with a hamza, from alata ya'iltuhu, with a fatha in the past tense and a kasra in the present. Abu Hatim preferred the reading of Abu 'Amr because of His saying: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾. Upon this reading is the saying of the poet:

Convey to Banu Asad from me a message, the clear statement of the message, neither deprived nor false.

Abu 'Ubaydah preferred the reading of the majority, and upon it is the saying of Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj:

A night, moist with dew, I travelled through, and Layth did not deprive me of its journey.

Both are eloquent dialects. ﴿Indeed Allah is Oft-Forgiving﴾, that is, abundant in forgiveness for whoever has committed a sin, ﴿Most Merciful﴾, abundant in mercy towards them.

Then, when He, glory be to Him, mentioned that those who said "We have believed" have not believed, and faith has not entered their hearts, He clarified the believers who deserve the name of faith applied to them, and He said: ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning sound faith, sincere, free from disagreement between heart and tongue. ﴿Then they have not doubted﴾, that is, nothing of doubt has entered their hearts, and no kind of uncertainty has mixed with them. ﴿And they strove with their wealth and their selves in the way of Allah﴾, that is, in His obedience and seeking His pleasure. Within striving (jihad) are included the righteous deeds that Allah has commanded, for they are among what a person strives against his self to perform and to sustain, as Allah, glory be to Him, commanded. The reference in His saying ﴿those﴾ is to those who combine the matters mentioned. It is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is His saying: ﴿They are the truthful﴾, that is, the truthful in attributing themselves to the quality of faith and entering among its people, not those other than them from among those who showed Islam with their tongues.

And he claimed to be a believer, but his heart was not at peace with faith, nor did its meaning reach him, nor did he act by the deeds of its people. These are the Bedouins mentioned earlier and the rest of the people of hypocrisy.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, commanded His Messenger to say to those Bedouins and their like another saying, since they claimed that they were believers. He said: ﴿Say: "Will you inform Allah of your religion?"﴾ The word "inform" (ta'lim) here means notification (i'lam), and for this reason the preposition bi (with) entered into "bi-dinikum", meaning: will you tell Him about it when you said "We have believed"? ﴿And Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth﴾, so how could the falsehood of what you claim of faith be hidden from Him? The sentence is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial clause from the object of "tu'allimuna". ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾; nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He knows what you conceal of disbelief and what you show of Islam out of fear of harm and hope for benefit.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, informed His Messenger of what they would say to him when they bestowed favour upon him by their claim of Islam. He said: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have submitted﴾, that is, they count their Islam as a favour upon you, since they said: "We came to you with our burdens and our dependents, and we did not fight you as Banu so-and-so and Banu so-and-so fought you." ﴿Say: "Do not consider your Islam a favour upon me"﴾, that is, do not count it a favour upon me, for Islam is the favour which its giver does not seek a reward for bestowing upon the one to whom it is granted. For this reason He said: ﴿Rather, Allah bestows favour upon you that He has guided you to faith﴾, that is, He directed you to it and showed you its path, straight, whether you reached the goal or did not reach it. The accusative of "your Islam" is either as the object of "yamunnuna" with the meaning of "ya'uddun" (they count), or by removing the preposition, meaning: because they submitted. Likewise His saying: ﴿that He has guided you to faith﴾, for it allows both possibilities. ﴿If you are truthful﴾ in what you claim, and the answer is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, meaning: if you are truthful, then the favour is Allah's upon you.

The majority read ﴿an hadakum﴾ with a fatha on an, and 'Asim read it with a kasra.

﴿Indeed Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, what is absent in them. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾; nothing of that is hidden from Him, so He will recompense you with good for good and with evil for evil.

The majority read ta'maluna in the second person, and Ibn Kathir read it in the third person.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il related from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: When the day of the conquest came, Bilal ascended and called the adhan on the Ka'bah. Some people said: "Is this black slave calling the adhan on the back of the Ka'bah?" Others said: "If Allah is displeased with this, He will change it." So this was revealed: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾.

Ibn al-Mundhir related a similar report from Ibn Jurayj.

Abu Dawud in his Marasil, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from al-Zuhri, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, commanded Banu Bayadah to marry a woman from among them to Abu Hind. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we marry our daughters to our clients (mawali)?" So this verse was revealed.

Ibn Mardawayh related from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab that this verse ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾ is Meccan, and it is specifically for the Arabs and the clients: which tribe they have, and which branches. And His saying ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ means: the most righteous of you in regard to shirk.

Al-Bukhari and Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: ash-shu'ub are the great tribes, and the qaba'il are the clans (butun).

al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him, who said: ash-shu'ub are the gatherings (jumma'), and the qaba'il are the thighs (afkhadh) by which they know one another.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir related from him also, who said: the qaba'il are the thighs, and the shu'ub are the masses (jumhur) like Mudar.

Al-Bukhari and others related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, was asked: "Who among people is the most noble?" He said: "The most noble of them with Allah is the most righteous of them." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "Then the most noble of people is Yusuf, the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the friend of Allah." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "Then are you asking me about the mines (ma'adin) of the Arabs?" They said: "Yes." He said: "The best of them in the Jahiliyyah are the best of them in Islam, when they have understanding." Hadiths have been related in the Sahih and elsewhere that piety is that by which servants are distinguished.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿The Bedouins say: "We have believed"﴾ that they were the Bedouins of Banu Asad and Khuzaymah, and regarding His saying ﴿But say: "We have submitted"﴾, that it was out of fear of killing and captivity.

Ibn Jarir related from Qatadah that it was revealed concerning Banu Asad. Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh related, and al-Suyuti said with a good chain, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa: "Some people from the Arabs said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we have submitted and we did not fight you as Banu so-and-so fought you.' So Allah revealed: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have submitted﴾."

al-Nasa'i, al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn 'Abbas something similar, and he mentioned that they were Banu Asad.

The benefit of mutual acquaintance (ta'aruf) is that each one of them is attributed to his own lineage and does not claim to be from another.

The intended meaning of this is that Allah, glory be to Him, created them thus for this benefit, not for boasting about their lineages and claiming that this people is better than that people, this tribe is more noble than that tribe, and this clan is more honourable than that clan.

Then He, glory be to Him, gave the reason for what the speech implies of the prohibition against boasting, and said: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most righteous of you﴾. That is, the distinction among you is only by piety (taqwa). Whoever is clothed with it is the one deserving to be more noble than the one who is not clothed with it, and more honourable and more excellent. So leave what you are engaged in of boasting about lineages, for that does not necessitate nobility, does not establish honour, and does not require superiority.

The majority read ﴿inna akramakum﴾ with a kasra on inna. Ibn 'Abbas read it with a fatha, meaning: because the most noble of you. ﴿Indeed Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of every thing known, including your deeds, ﴿All-Aware﴾ of what you conceal and what you disclose; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

When He, glory be to Him, mentioned that the most noble of people with Allah is the most pious of them towards Him, and the root of piety is faith (iman), He mentioned what the Arabs used to claim of faith in order to establish for them nobility and excellence, and He said: ﴿The Bedouins say: "We have believed."﴾ They were Banu Asad, who showed Islam in a year of drought, wanting charity. So Allah, glory be to Him, commanded His Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, to respond to them, and He said: ﴿Say: "You have not believed"﴾. That is, you have not affirmed with a sound affirmation that comes from conviction of the heart, sincerity of intention, and tranquillity. ﴿But say: "We have submitted"﴾, that is, we have surrendered (istaslamna) out of fear of killing and captivity, or out of greed for charity. This is the description of the hypocrites, for they showed submission outwardly while their hearts did not believe. For this reason He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾. That is, what you have shown with your tongues was not in agreement with your hearts, but was merely a saying with the tongue without sound belief or sincere intention. The sentence is either a new sentence to confirm what precedes it, or it is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal). In (lamma) there is the meaning of expectation (tawaqqu').

Al-Zajjaj said: Islam is the manifestation of submission and acceptance of what the Prophet brought, and by it blood is protected. If with that outward manifestation there is conviction and affirmation in the heart, then that is faith and its possessor is a believer.

He has removed these people from faith by His saying: ﴿And faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾, that is, you have not affirmed, and you have only submitted to protect yourselves from killing. ﴿But if you obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ with sound obedience proceeding from sincere intentions and hearts that affirm, not hypocritical, ﴿He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds﴾. It is said: lata yalitu, when it decreases; and latahu yaliituhu and yalutuhu, when it reduces it. The meaning is: He will not reduce anything of your deeds for you.

The majority read ﴿yalitkum﴾ from lataha yaliituhu, like baa'a yabee'uhu.

Abu 'Amr read ﴿la ya'iltkum﴾ with a hamza, from alata ya'iltuhu, with a fatha in the past tense and a kasra in the present. Abu Hatim preferred the reading of Abu 'Amr because of His saying: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾. Upon this reading is the saying of the poet:

Convey to Banu Asad from me a message, the clear statement of the message, neither deprived nor false.

Abu 'Ubaydah preferred the reading of the majority, and upon it is the saying of Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj:

A night, moist with dew, I travelled through, and Layth did not deprive me of its journey.

Both are eloquent dialects. ﴿Indeed Allah is Oft-Forgiving﴾, that is, abundant in forgiveness for whoever has committed a sin, ﴿Most Merciful﴾, abundant in mercy towards them.

Then, when He, glory be to Him, mentioned that those who said "We have believed" have not believed, and faith has not entered their hearts, He clarified the believers who deserve the name of faith applied to them, and He said: ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning sound faith, sincere, free from disagreement between heart and tongue. ﴿Then they have not doubted﴾, that is, nothing of doubt has entered their hearts, and no kind of uncertainty has mixed with them. ﴿And they strove with their wealth and their selves in the way of Allah﴾, that is, in His obedience and seeking His pleasure. Within striving (jihad) are included the righteous deeds that Allah has commanded, for they are among what a person strives against his self to perform and to sustain, as Allah, glory be to Him, commanded. The reference in His saying ﴿those﴾ is to those who combine the matters mentioned. It is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is His saying: ﴿They are the truthful﴾, that is, the truthful in attributing themselves to the quality of faith and entering among its people, not those other than them from among those who showed Islam with their tongues.

And he claimed to be a believer, but his heart was not at peace with faith, nor did its meaning reach him, nor did he act by the deeds of its people. These are the Bedouins mentioned earlier and the rest of the people of hypocrisy.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, commanded His Messenger to say to those Bedouins and their like another saying, since they claimed that they were believers. He said: ﴿Say: "Will you inform Allah of your religion?"﴾ The word "inform" (ta'lim) here means notification (i'lam), and for this reason the preposition bi (with) entered into "bi-dinikum", meaning: will you tell Him about it when you said "We have believed"? ﴿And Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth﴾, so how could the falsehood of what you claim of faith be hidden from Him? The sentence is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial clause from the object of "tu'allimuna". ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾; nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He knows what you conceal of disbelief and what you show of Islam out of fear of harm and hope for benefit.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, informed His Messenger of what they would say to him when they bestowed favour upon him by their claim of Islam. He said: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have submitted﴾, that is, they count their Islam as a favour upon you, since they said: "We came to you with our burdens and our dependents, and we did not fight you as Banu so-and-so and Banu so-and-so fought you." ﴿Say: "Do not consider your Islam a favour upon me"﴾, that is, do not count it a favour upon me, for Islam is the favour which its giver does not seek a reward for bestowing upon the one to whom it is granted. For this reason He said: ﴿Rather, Allah bestows favour upon you that He has guided you to faith﴾, that is, He directed you to it and showed you its path, straight, whether you reached the goal or did not reach it. The accusative of "your Islam" is either as the object of "yamunnuna" with the meaning of "ya'uddun" (they count), or by removing the preposition, meaning: because they submitted. Likewise His saying: ﴿that He has guided you to faith﴾, for it allows both possibilities. ﴿If you are truthful﴾ in what you claim, and the answer is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, meaning: if you are truthful, then the favour is Allah's upon you.

The majority read ﴿an hadakum﴾ with a fatha on an, and 'Asim read it with a kasra.

﴿Indeed Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, what is absent in them. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾; nothing of that is hidden from Him, so He will recompense you with good for good and with evil for evil.

The majority read ta'maluna in the second person, and Ibn Kathir read it in the third person.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il related from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: When the day of the conquest came, Bilal ascended and called the adhan on the Ka'bah. Some people said: "Is this black slave calling the adhan on the back of the Ka'bah?" Others said: "If Allah is displeased with this, He will change it." So this was revealed: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾.

Ibn al-Mundhir related a similar report from Ibn Jurayj.

Abu Dawud in his Marasil, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from al-Zuhri, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, commanded Banu Bayadah to marry a woman from among them to Abu Hind. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we marry our daughters to our clients (mawali)?" So this verse was revealed.

Ibn Mardawayh related from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab that this verse ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾ is Meccan, and it is specifically for the Arabs and the clients: which tribe they have, and which branches. And His saying ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ means: the most righteous of you in regard to shirk.

Al-Bukhari and Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: ash-shu'ub are the great tribes, and the qaba'il are the clans (butun).

al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him, who said: ash-shu'ub are the gatherings (jumma'), and the qaba'il are the thighs (afkhadh) by which they know one another.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir related from him also, who said: the qaba'il are the thighs, and the shu'ub are the masses (jumhur) like Mudar.

Al-Bukhari and others related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, was asked: "Who among people is the most noble?" He said: "The most noble of them with Allah is the most righteous of them." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "Then the most noble of people is Yusuf, the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the friend of Allah." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "Then are you asking me about the mines (ma'adin) of the Arabs?" They said: "Yes." He said: "The best of them in the Jahiliyyah are the best of them in Islam, when they have understanding." Hadiths have been related in the Sahih and elsewhere that piety is that by which servants are distinguished.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿The Bedouins say: "We have believed"﴾ that they were the Bedouins of Banu Asad and Khuzaymah, and regarding His saying ﴿But say: "We have submitted"﴾, that it was out of fear of killing and captivity.

Ibn Jarir related from Qatadah that it was revealed concerning Banu Asad. Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh related, and al-Suyuti said with a good chain, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa: "Some people from the Arabs said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we have submitted and we did not fight you as Banu so-and-so fought you.' So Allah revealed: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have submitted﴾."

al-Nasa'i, al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn 'Abbas something similar, and he mentioned that they were Banu Asad.
